text:
marta: Quick heads-up — we're seeing a mid-latency regression on long-prefix Llama workloads after the kernel-scheduler change rolled out in v2.2. Anyone else notice this?

devin: saw a blip in nightly graphs. Which models/seq lengths are affected?

marta: Primarily Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B on 2k+ prefix traces. Qwen appears fine. Numbers from the nightly: p50 +12ms, p95 ~+40ms, p99 +80ms for 2048-prefix samples. Batch sizes same.

ryan: tagging perf-bot and asha :eyes: Could be KV-cache prefetch/eviction interaction — v2.2 switched to the "aggressive-freeslots" eviction policy which increases churn for long prefixes.

marta: attaching short profiler snapshot (relevant lines):
```
[perf] 2026-03-12T10:45:12Z model=llama-2-13b seq=2048
kernel_runner: switches=132 -> 188 (v2.1 -> v2.2)
kv_cache: evictions=812 -> 2420
cpu_ms: user=23 -> 34
latency_ms: p50=54 -> 66, p99=420 -> 500
```

devin: that many kernel switches is suspicious. Scheduler seems preferring smaller-kernel variants more often which adds context switch overhead.

asha: I ran a focused microbenchmark. Soft-evict (age-weighted LRU) reduces p99 by ~30ms on 2k-prefix, but increases memory footprint by ~180-220MB per pod. Short config gist: `kvcache.eviction = "age_weighted_lru"`, `kvcache.soft_threshold_pct = 60`, `kvcache.precision = "bf16"`.

devin: BF16 for KV caches helps memory+stability, but curious about FP8 — were there quality regressions?

asha: For KV specifically, bf16 is safe across Llama/Mistral. FP8 quantized KV gives bigger memory wins but we observed rare next-token probability drift on Llama-architectures when head_kv_dim isn't an even multiple for the quantizer. Example micro-delta:
```
cfg: fp16_kv vs fp8_kv on llama-2-13b seq=2048
- logprob delta mean: -0.0021 (negligible)
- token disagreement rate: 0.18% -> 0.9% (fp8)
- BLEU-ish synthetic metric drop ~0.4pts (edge cases)
```
Recommend bf16 for production KV unless we do model-specific fp8 sanity checks.

ryan: On the kernel side, scheduler v2.2 uses `max_queue_time` weighting to pick kernel variant. With long prefixes the histogram shifts and it starts bouncing between kernel variants more. Proposal: add a "kernel-stability" penalty that prefers the same kernel used for previous chunk unless expected gain > threshold. Also bias selection by recent sequence-length histogram window (last 5k requests).

marta: Good idea. Operational ask: can we roll a 5% canary with `scheduler.prefer_stability=true` and `kvcache.eviction=age_weighted_lru` and keep `kvcache.precision=bf16`? I'll open the rollout ticket.

perf-bot: Canary rollout queued: 5% on shared-dedicated. Predicted: cost +3% (memory), latency delta (canary preds) p50 -3ms, p99 -25ms for long-prefix workloads. CI link: http://ci.internal/redwood/canary/1768123456

devin: lgtm. Add a regression test to perf-suite: `long_prefix_stability_test` that runs Llama/Mistral/Mixtral at 1k/2k/4k prefixes and verifies kernel-switch count and kv-eviction rates.

marta: Added PR r/eng-runtime#987 with canary config and the new perf test. Will monitor canary dashboards and post follow-ups in this thread.

ryan: one more note — for Mixtral we should keep prefetch enabled but lower prefetch depth when using age_weighted_lru; prefetch + aggressive eviction was the worst combo.

asha: ack. I'll prepare a small config matrix for per-model defaults (llama: bf16+age_weighted_lru+stability=true, mistral: bf16+moderate-prefetch, mixtral: bf16+low-prefetch+stability).

marta: thanks all — will report back after 12h canary window.
